correctness.rationale: The proof groups all pole layers whose Selberg--Delange expansions can overlap via z_{r+m/2}=z_r-1, proves the first fractional group is not identically zero using Walsh--Hadamard linear independence of the Euler products, and then obtains a unique nonzero leading exponent after accounting for finite vanishing orders at s=1. Integer pole-order layers are lower than every algebraic logarithmic order. The coordinatewise corollary uses the cited positivity of the weight-one constants.

originality.rationale: Tang arXiv:2609.16716v1 explicitly states pairwise strict bias in the binary setting as a conjecture and proves only extremal comparisons plus numerical examples. Exact, synonymous, Fourier/Walsh, and Selberg--Delange searches found no prior proof or stronger coverage. The source is very recent, so unindexed contemporaneous work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the full stated binary strict-bias conjecture and strengthens it with a quantized family of pairwise bias exponents and an explicit Boolean-lattice monotonicity law.
